source.title: Abhinavagupta: self-awareness is the nature of consciousness, not the result of cognition
source.author: Codex/Hermes loop

claims.claim_text: Self-awareness (svasaṃvedana) is the nature (svabhāva) of consciousness, not a result (phala) produced by cognition. Consciousness is self-luminous (svaprakāśa) and is its own object of awareness; it is not an object of a means of knowledge other than its own self-awareness.
claims.hetu: consciousness is self-luminous and not dependent on any external means of knowledge
claims.sadhya: self-awareness is the nature of consciousness, not a result
claims.vyapti_statement: If consciousness is self-luminous and its own object, then self-awareness is its nature, not a product of cognition.

falsifier.condition: Show that the Buddhist phala model of self-awareness is compatible with consciousness being self-luminous — i.e., that the result-of-cognition account does not undermine intrinsic self-awareness.
